title: Methylation Specific Multiplex Droplet PCR using Polymer Droplet Generator Device for Hematological Diagnostics
protocol: Thaw frozen human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) by placing the cryovial in a water bath at 37°C for 5 min.
Invert the cryovial twice to gently resuspend the cells.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 15 mL conical tube using a 1 mL pipette.
Add 10 mL of pre-warmed (37°C) growth medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (RPMI-1640 + 10% FBS) to the 15 mL tube containing the PBMCs.
Centrifuge the cell suspension in a swinging bucket centrifuge at room temperature at a speed of 330 x g for 10 min with rapid acceleration and high brake setting.
Carefully decant the supernatant after the spin is over.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 3 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) pH 7.2, containing 2 mM ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA).
Mix the cells by inverting the tube with the cap tightly closed.
Prepare two 1.5 mL microtubes and using a pipette, aliquot 1.5 mL of the cell suspension in each tube.
Use one tube for subsequent immunofluorescence staining and another for DNA extraction.
Resuspend cells in 200 μL of PBS buffer containing 0.1% sodium azide and 2% FBS.
Adjust the final concentration of the cell suspension to a maximum of 2 x 10^7 cells/mL.
Divide the cell suspension into two separate 1.5 mL microtubes, each with 100 μL volume.
Add 20 μL volume of anti-Hu CD3/CD4 conjugated with FITC and PE to one tube.
Add 20 μL volume of anti-Hu CD4/CD25 conjugated with FITC and PE to the second tube.
Add 1 drop of blue fluorescent live cell stain to each tube.
Incubate at room temperature using a tube rotator for 2 h, protecting from light.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at room temperature at 330 x g for 10 min with rapid acceleration and brake on high.
Decant the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet by tapping the tube carefully.
Add 1 mL of PBS, pH 7.2 containing 2 mM EDTA to each tube.
Mix cells by inverting the tubes twice.
Repeat steps 2.6 and 2.7 for three times.
Resuspend cells in 20 μL of PBS pH 7.2 containing 2 mM EDTA.
Pipette 10 μL drop of the cell suspension onto a borosilicate microscope slide.
Wait for 2 min for cells to slowly sediment to the bottom of the drop.
Carefully place a glass cover slip on top of the microscope slide.
Place the slide on the stage of an inverted microscope.
Record images of cells using a 10x objective and an EMCCD camera connected to the microscope for each fluorophore in both cell suspension samples.
Manually count fluorescently labeled cells (see Supplementary Information for raw data).
Take the ratio of anti-Hu CD3 and anti-Hu CD4/CD25 labeled-cells to DAPI-stained cells to obtain proportions of CD3+ T-Cells and CD4+ CD25+ T-Regs to total leukocytes.
Extract DNA from PBMCs prepared in section 1 using a magnetic DNA purification kit following the manufacturer's procedures.
In a 1.5 mL tube, suspend cells in 100 µL of PBS and add 20 µL of Proteinase K and 400 µL of Lysis/Binding buffer.
Mix by pipetting up-down 10x.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Capture the DNA-bead complex by placing the tube on a magnetic rack for 1-2 min, then carefully remove and discard the supernatant.
Remove the tube containing the DNA-bead complex from the magnetic rack and resuspend the beads in 600 µL of Wash Buffer #1 to wash away any non-specific binding.
Place the tube again on the magnetic rack and carefully remove and discard the supernatant.
Repeat steps with 600 µL of Wash Buffer #2.
Leave the tube open to air-dry for 1 min.
Remove the tube from the magnetic rack and elute the DNA by dispensing 100 µL of Elution Buffer.
Pipette the DNA/bead complex up and down 20x.
Place the tube containing the eluted DNA on a magnetic rack and incubate for 1-2 minutes to separate the magnetic beads from the eluted DNA.
Transfer the eluted purified DNA solution to a new clean tube.
Assess the concentration of the purified DNA sample by measuring the absorbance at 260 nm using a spectrophotometer.
To 20 µL of DNA sample (200-500 ng) in a PCR tube, add 130 µL of Conversion Reagent.
Mix well and spin down briefly.
Transfer the PCR tube to a thermal cycler and perform cycling at 98 °C for 8 minutes.
Perform cycling at 54 °C for 60 minutes and hold at 4 °C.
Add 600 µL of Binding Buffer to an ion chromatography (IC) column placed into a collection tube.
Add the DNA sample to the IC column containing the binding buffer and mix by inverting the tube several times.
Centrifuge for 30 seconds at full speed.
Discard the collected flow-through.
To the column, add 100 µL of Wash Buffer.
Perform centrifugation as described previously and discard the flow-through.
Add 200 µL of Desulfonation Buffer to the column.
Incubate at room temperature for 15-20 minutes.
Centrifuge and discard the flow-through as described previously.
Add 200 µL of Wash Buffer to the column.
Centrifuge at full speed for 30 seconds and discard the flow-through.
Repeat step involving adding 200 µL of Wash Buffer to the column.
Transfer the column to a new 1.5 mL collection tube.
Add 100 µL of PCR-grade water on the membrane of the column.
Centrifuge at full speed for 1 min to elute the DNA.
Assess the concentration of bisulfite-converted DNA sample by measuring the absorbance at 260 nm using a spectrophotometer.
Store DNA at -20 °C for short term storage or at -70 °C for long term storage.
Clean a 6” silicon wafer using oxygen plasma at 500 W for 10 s.
Spin-coat SU-8 resist onto the silicon wafer at 900 rpm for 40 s to achieve a total film thickness of 100 µm.
Place the wafer on a hot plate and pre-bake for 15 min at 65 °C, followed by 2 h at 95 °C.
Expose to UV light at 365 nm through a high-definition transparency photomask using an exposure dose of 1,000 mJ/cm².
Place the wafer on a hot plate and post-bake for 15 min at 65 °C, followed by 40 min at 95 °C.
Develop by immersing in propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate (PGMEA) for 5 min.
Rinse with PGMEA.
Rinse with isopropanol.
Dry with a stream of nitrogen gas.
Place the wafer on a hot plate.
Hard-bake the wafer for 2 hours at 135 °C.
Silanize the wafer in a vacuum desiccator containing trichloro perfluorooctyl silane.
Mix PDMS prepolymers at a ratio of 10:1 w/w of elastomer base to curing agent.
Place the mixture in a planetary centrifugal vacuum mixer for mixing and degassing.
Pour the mixed PDMS onto the mold placed in a custom metal holder.
Cure the PDMS mixture at 65 °C for 2 hours.
Peel off the PDMS mold from the SU-8 master using tweezers.
Prepare epoxy resin using a ratio of 100/83 w/w of resin to hardener.
Degas the epoxy mixture under reduced pressure in a vacuum drying oven for 30 minutes.
Pour the degassed epoxy resin over the PDMS replica.
Cure the epoxy resin at 80 °C for 12 hours.
Remove the cured epoxy mold from the PDMS replica.
Place the epoxy mold on a hot plate.
Hard-bake the epoxy mold at 120 °C for 2 hours.
Extrude TPE pellets at 165 °C into sheets.
Cut the TPE sheet from the roll using scissors into a 7” square.
Place the TPE sheet between the epoxy mold and a non-patterned silanized silicon wafer.
Perform hot-embossing at 125 °C, an applied force of 10 kN, and a pressure of 10–2 mbar for 10 min.
Demold the embossed TPE carefully using methanol spray.
Cut another 7” square sheet of TPE and place it between two non-patterned silanized silicon wafers.
Perform hot-embossing at 140 °C, an applied force of 10 kN, and a pressure of 10–2 mbar for 10 min to form a planar surface.
Demold the embossed TPE carefully using methanol spray.
Cut each of the embossed TPE sheets to device size using a doctor blade.
Punch access holes for inlet and outlet channels in the structured device using a 1 mm biopsy punch needle with a plunger.
Enclose the channels by placing a planar TPE device in direct contact with the channels at room temperature.
Optionally, place in an oven at 70 °C for 2 h to promote device bonding.
Fit the access holes with a disposable fluidic tubing (I.D. 0.25 mm, O.D. 0.8 mm).
Seal the joints using an epoxy glue to ensure leak-proof manipulation.
Thaw all components of the master mix except for the enzyme mix.
Mix the master mix thoroughly by pipetting up-down and spin down briefly.
Add 1 μL of bisulfite converted DNA to master mix in a PCR tube.
Mix the reaction by pipetting up-down and spin down briefly.
Prefill one precision glass syringe with 250 μL of carrier oil containing 5% fluoro-surfactant.
Prefill another precision glass syringe with 50 µL of carrier oil before loading 100 µL of the PCR mix to ensure dispensing of the entire sample volume during emulsification.
Set-up a droplet microfluidic device on a stage of an upright light microscope equipped with a high-speed camera to observe and record droplet formation in real-time.
Place prefilled syringes onto the programmable syringe pump.
Connect tubing from the syringes to the inlet channels of the droplet microfluidic device using PEEK union with fittings.
Place tubing from the outlet of the droplet generator inside a 0.5 mL PCR tube.
Adjust flow rate of the syringe pump to 2 µL/min.
Allow droplet size to stabilize before collecting emulsion.
Collect 75 μL of emulsion and transfer it to a 0.2 mL PCR tube for thermal cycling.
Ensure oil content in PCR tube matches volume of dispersed phase to prevent coalescence during thermal cycling.
Place the 0.2 mL PCR tube into the thermal cycler.
Perform preheating at 95 °C for 5 min.
Proceed with 45 cycles: denaturation at 95 °C for 15 s followed by annealing/extension at 60 °C for 30 s.
Use remaining emulsion to fill a borosilicate capillary tube (100 μm depth) with a rectangular profile.
Place the filled borosilicate tube on a microscope slide.
Record bright field images of droplets using an inverted microscope equipped with an EMCCD camera and 10x objective.
Measure droplet diameter using image analysis software.
Set the scale of known distance in microns corresponding to the number of pixels in the image.
Convert the image to grayscale.
Adjust brightness and contrast if needed.
Set a manual threshold to delineate and fill the circles.
Analyze the particles by setting the circularity to 0.75 – 1.
Compute the mean droplet diameter assuming a spherical droplet.
Estimate the partition volume for calculating absolute target concentration.

Ensure that the droplets are monodisperse by analyzing the coefficient of variation (CV) which is taken as the ratio of the standard deviations to the mean values (k = 1), for the droplet diameter (< 3%).
Transfer the PCR emulsion into a borosilicate capillary tube with a rectangular profile.
Fix the filled capillaries on a microscope slide and seal both sides using UV acrylic adhesive.
Apply a UV light source on the UV adhesive carefully to avoid illuminating the emulsion.
Load the glass slide on an inverted microscope equipped with an EMCCD camera and a 10x objective.
Select Acquire | Live - Fast in the microscope imaging software to start real-time camera acquisition.
Observe the sample and ensure that the width of the capillary is captured.
Set the bright field lamp for diascopic illumination at 3.5 V.
Set the broad-spectrum LED fluorescent lamp for episcopic illumination at 20% intensity.
Select Calibration | Optical Configurations command in the imaging software to adjust capture settings for all wavelengths (Bright field, FAM, HEX and Cy5).
Switch the corresponding fluorescence filter cube manually for each fluorophore.
Use a filter cube for bright field imaging to keep the same optical path.
Adjust the exposure time manually prior to image acquisition using Acquire | Camera Settings command for each fluorophore as summarized in Table 3.
Set the readout mode EM gain 17 MHz at 16-bit with a gain multiplier of 100 in the ‘Capture Settings’ menu of the software.
In the LUT window, set the LUTs scale such that the transmission signal is encompassed within the set range from 500 up to 12,000 approximately.
Automate the capture using a multipoint acquisition program with both XY scan and multiple wavelength options.
Set up the XY scan in the XY scan menu of the software.
Choose the large image definition box in ‘Custom Multipoint Definition’ and set it to 40.0 x 1.0 mm.
Use 1% overlap for the XY scan.
Enable the ‘Use Focus Surface’ option.
Adjust the focus plane at different points on the sample using the focus knob.
Set up the multiple wavelength scan by selecting the scan tab.
Add each of the optical configurations created in step 6.1.7 for each wavelength.
Click to close active shutter during stage movement and during filter change.
Start the acquisition by pressing the ‘Start Run’ button.
Export each acquisition frame into tiff files.
Split each channel into a separated file using split multiple files option.
Apply saved LUTs settings when splitting channels.
Use point name and channel name option to differentiate image files.
Sort all acquired images by brightfield and fluorescence filters.
Upload sorted images to an open source image analysis software.
Use image analysis software to create a pipeline.
Upload brightfield and fluorescence tiff images.
Add module ‘ColorToGray’.
Add module ‘IdentifyPrimaryObjects’.
Add module ‘MeasureObjectIntensity’.
Add module ‘ExportToSpreadsheet’.
Use brightfield droplet images to identify objects.
Use identified objects as mask to measure intensity of fluorescent images.
Run pipeline with selected tiff images to extract average fluorescence intensity.
Conduct the experiment in triplicate.
Each set consists of ~5,000 droplets for analysis.
Apply the ‘definetherain’ algorithm to identify positive and negative droplet clusters.
Determine threshold intensity of positive droplets within 3 standard deviations of the mean.
Use image analysis software to implement a new pipeline.
Set fluorescence threshold for each gene target as defined previously.
Upload brightfield and fluorescent images to pipeline.

Add module ‘RescaleIntensity’.
Add module ‘Threshold’.
Add module ‘IdentifyPrimaryObjects’.
Add module ‘MeasureObjectSizeShape’.
Add module ‘FilterObjects’.

Create unique modules for brightfield images and each fluorescence filter for droplets.
Rescale image intensity scale from 0 to 1 for each fluorescence image group.
Set the threshold to identify and count objects above the established threshold.
Shrink objects if necessary using an ‘ExpandOrShrinkObjects’ module.
Identify objects within a size range of 20-30 pixels.
Filter counted objects to retain those with a diameter in the 75 µm range.
Retain objects with a round spherical eccentricity of 0.5 and below.
Export results to a table listing total droplet count from brightfield images.
Include droplet counts for Cy5 fluorescence channel for C-LESS gene.
Include droplet counts for HEX fluorescence channel for methylated CD3Z gene.
Include droplet counts for FAM fluorescence channel for methylated FOXP3 gene.
Calculate the ratio of negative droplets for each gene target.
Apply Poisson distribution to obtain copies per droplet (CPD).
Calculate absolute target concentration using CPD and droplet volume.
